specification.problem: Given a 4-bit reversible function pi (permutation of {0..15}), find a Toffoli network (NOT, CNOT, TOF3, TOF4) realizing pi with minimum quantum cost QC, and build the corresponding measurement-free unitary U_pi.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny explicit 4-bit permutation, classical offline Dijkstra search over the Cayley graph of the NCT-plus-TOF4 gate library, then compilation of the resulting network to x, cx, ccx, mcx gates. The paper's actual gate-count-optimal tool, its benchmarks and the 74% saving are out of scope.

symbols.meaning: 4-bit input integer, x=sum_i x_i 2^i, qubit q_i holds x_i (little-endian)
library gate viewed as a permutation of {0..15}
symbols.domain: set of NOT, CNOT, TOF3, TOF4 on 4 wires with all control/target choices

symbols.meaning: standard quantum cost of gate g
total quantum cost of network C

equations.label: Permutation unitary
equations.description: Target unitary mapping each basis state to its image under pi, little-endian encoding.
equations.justification: Standard encoding of a reversible function as a unitary; chosen for the tiny instance, not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Network composition
equations.description: A Toffoli network realizes pi as a product of gate permutations.
equations.justification: Background on reversible circuits composed of Toffoli-class gates.

equations.label: Quantum cost of a network
equations.description: Additive cost model with the commonly used standard costs.
equations.justification: Common NCT quantum cost values recalled from background; the abstract only mentions quantum cost (QC).

equations.label: QC-minimal synthesis
equations.description: Dijkstra on the Cayley graph of S_16 with edge weight qc(g), starting from the identity, until pi is reached.
equations.justification: The abstract states the goal of reducing QC with an exact gate-count tool; the Dijkstra search is a proposed stand-in for the tool, whose internals are unknown.
assumptions: the search replaces the paper's tool

equations.label: Saving percentage
equations.description: Relative quantum cost saving versus a baseline circuit.
equations.abstract_quote: savings in QC of up to 74% comparing with previously known circuits
equations.justification: The percentage saving is inferred from the abstract's claim; the exact formula is the standard definition.

registers.name: q
registers.role: data qubits q0..q3, little-endian; computational basis state |x> maps to |pi(x)>

specification.initial_state: Any computational basis state |x>, x in 0..15, or the full basis for unitary verification; no ancillas.

steps.description: Fix a small instance pi, for example a 4-bit permutation given explicitly, and a baseline GC-optimal network.
Assign standard quantum costs to the gates and compute the baseline QC.
Run Dijkstra over permutations with the gate library to find the min-QC network for pi.
Compile the chosen network to x, cx, ccx, mcx gates, measurement-free, and check U|x>=|pi(x)> for all 16 x. Compute the saving.

specification.measurement: None in the circuit; the output is decoded by reading the computational basis state as pi(x) (little-endian).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Offline classical search for the min-QC network and calculation of the saving percentage.
assumptions: Tiny explicit instance chosen by the team, not from the abstract
Dijkstra search stands in for the paper's optimal-synthesis tool
